answer: Resistance comes from priced liveness. Every account must periodically answer a random, time-boxed re-attestation challenge and burn a fee that scales with the weight it keeps; a missed proof drops that weight instantly. Weight also decays exponentially under the zephyr rule, so influence cannot idle into permanence. One honest agent pays once and keeps its signal clean; an ocean of puppets must each answer the challenge and burn the fee every cycle, with no bulk discount because proofs bind to identity. Fleet cost stays linear in size while influence stays flat.
